name: Matcha

harvest.window: shaded first flush, stone-milled from tencha

pluckStandard: same shaded leaf as gyokuro, destemmed and deveined

processing.description: Like gyokuro, then dried without rolling — that unswept leaf is tencha.
蒸青, then the leaf is dried as flakes. No 揉捻.

Tencha ground to matcha. The term “ceremonial grade” has no legal or industry definition in Japan or anywhere else — it is export marketing. Leaf grade and mill freshness are what you can actually check.

taste: usucha: frothy umami; koicha: dense sweet broth
profile.mouthfeel: suspension, not an infusion — the leaf is drunk

water.note: Soft, ~75 °C. Sift the powder. Koicha wants even better leaf than usucha.

storage: Freezer, then fridge; small tins. Matcha dies in weeks once opened.

shelfLife.note: Warm the sealed packet to room temperature before opening.

compare.differentiator: They share shade and steam. Matcha is never rolled; gyokuro is kneaded. That missing 揉捻 is the whole distinction.
Tencha is the unswept leaf. Matcha is that leaf put through a stone mill.

summary: Stone-milled shaded tencha: usucha froth and koicha paste are two ratios of the same powder.
